name: NR (Nicotinamide Riboside)
desc: NR is a legitimate NAD+ precursor with human RCT data. TNiC standardizes on NMN for stack integration, but NR is defensible if your physician prefers it or you already respond. Never combine high-dose NR + NMN without oversight.
pathway: NR → NMN → NAD+ → Sirtuin axis

name: Rapamycin (Sirolimus)
desc: Rapamycin inhibits mTORC1, the nutrient-sensing kinase that blocks autophagy. It is the most replicated pharmacological lifespan extension in mice — but human longevity use is off-label, prescription-only, and immunosuppressive at continuous doses. Tier B: strong preclinical + emerging human safety; no completed human longevity RCT. Physician supervision is mandatory.
mechanism: When nutrients and growth signals are abundant, **mTOR Complex 1 (mTORC1)** prioritizes protein synthesis and cell growth over repair. With age, this balance skews toward growth signaling — autophagy, mitophagy, and stress resistance stay suppressed even when cells need cleanup.
pathway: mTORC1 ↔ AMPK seesaw

name: TUDCA (Tauroursodeoxycholic Acid)
desc: TUDCA is a taurine-conjugated bile acid that acts as a chemical chaperone, stabilizing protein folding and reducing ER stress. Tier B: strong preclinical proteostasis and mitochondrial data; human hepatoprotection studies exist but no longevity RCT. Start 250–500 mg/day, titrate to 500–1000 mg over 8–12 weeks; retest ALT/AST at week 8.
mechanism: Aging cells accumulate **misfolded proteins**. The unfolded protein response (UPR) tries to correct folding, but chronic ER stress triggers CHOP-mediated apoptosis and inflammatory signaling. Proteostasis fails — aggregates rise, mitochondria lose membrane integrity, autophagy stalls on damage control instead of productive clearance.
pathway: ER stress → TUDCA intervention

name: Grape Seed Extract (95% OPC)
desc: Grape seed extract standardized to ≥95% oligomeric proanthocyanidins (OPC) is a well-studied polyphenol antioxidant with real human RCT support for vascular health. A 2016 meta-analysis of 16 trials found a significant systolic blood-pressure reduction, and diastolic-BP and heart-rate benefits replicate in later analyses; effects track with dose and OPC standardization, so the form genuinely matters. A strong educational pick when you're building an antioxidant and vascular-support layer.
mechanism: Grape seed extract is a polyphenol concentrate rich in oligomeric proanthocyanidins (OPCs) — chains of catechin/epicatechin units found in the seeds of *Vitis vinifera*. Standardization matters here more than for most botanicals: unstandardized extracts vary enormously in actual OPC content, and the human trials behind this compound were run on extracts standardized to roughly 95% OPC — a product labeled simply "grape seed extract" without that standardization is not necessarily comparable.
pathway: Proposed mechanism (polyphenol pharmacology)

name: Cocoa Flavanols
desc: Cocoa flavanols are among the best-studied dietary compounds for the aging vascular system. They raise nitric-oxide availability, improve flow-mediated dilation, and lower blood pressure across dozens of RCTs — and in COSMOS, the largest trial (~21,000 adults), they cut cardiovascular deaths in the pre-specified secondary analysis. A genuinely strong, food-derived way to support endothelial health. 500–900 mg total flavanols/day, standardized.
mechanism: The endothelium — the single-cell lining of every blood vessel — stiffens and loses nitric-oxide output with age, and that decline sits upstream of much of cardiovascular aging. Cocoa flavanols (chiefly epicatechin) are one of the most reliably vasoactive nutrients we have: a large Cochrane review of 40+ RCTs found consistent, if modest, blood-pressure lowering, and the 2022 COSMOS trial (n≈21,000) reported a **27% reduction in cardiovascular death** in its pre-specified secondary endpoint. That is real, large-scale human signal for a compound you can get from food.
pathway: Among the best-studied nutrients for the aging vascular system — NO, blood pressure, and a cardiovascular-death signal in COSMOS

name: Citrus Bergamot
desc: Citrus bergamot is a polyphenol-rich extract with real human RCTs showing meaningful drops in LDL and triglycerides and a rise in HDL — a genuinely useful, non-statin lever for lipids and metabolic health. It works through the same HMG-CoA pathway statins target, plus AMPK activation. 500–1,000 mg/day standardized to flavonoids.
mechanism: Bergamot (*Citrus bergamia*) concentrates a distinctive set of flavonoids — brutieridin and melitidin — that behave like natural HMG-CoA reductase modulators. In human trials it lowers total and LDL cholesterol, drops triglycerides, and nudges HDL upward, often by double-digit percentages. For anyone building a metabolic or cardiovascular layer without (or alongside) a statin, that is a strong, well-tolerated option.
pathway: A polyphenol lipid lever with real RCTs lowering LDL and triglycerides — statin-like pathway, no prescription

name: L-Theanine
desc: L-theanine is the amino acid in green tea that produces calm, focused alertness without sedation. Human EEG and cognitive studies show it raises alpha-wave activity and, paired with caffeine, sharpens attention while smoothing the jitter. A clean, fast-acting, extremely safe nootropic. 100–200 mg, on its own or with caffeine.
mechanism: Chronic stress and poor attention are quietly corrosive to healthspan — they drive cortisol, disrupt sleep, and erode cognition. L-theanine is one of the few supplements with a genuinely reliable acute effect here: within 30–40 minutes it shifts the brain toward an alert-but-relaxed state, measured directly as increased alpha-wave power. It is the reason a cup of green tea feels calmer than the same caffeine from coffee.
pathway: Calm, focused alertness without sedation — the most replicable acute nootropic, and it tames caffeine jitter

name: Collagen Peptides
desc: Hydrolyzed collagen peptides are one of the best-evidenced supplements for the visible and structural side of aging: human RCTs show improved skin elasticity and hydration, reduced joint pain, and support for bone density. The peptides act as both building blocks and signals that tell fibroblasts and chondrocytes to build. 10–15 g/day.
mechanism: Collagen is the scaffolding of skin, tendon, cartilage, and bone, and its synthesis falls with age — which shows up as thinner skin, achier joints, and weaker bone. Hydrolyzed collagen delivers a distinctive pool of glycine, proline, and hydroxyproline plus specific bioactive di- and tri-peptides that survive digestion, reach connective tissue, and stimulate the cells there to build new matrix. The result is a supplement with unusually direct, visible payoffs.
pathway: One of the best-evidenced supplements for skin elasticity, joint comfort, and bone — building blocks that also signal repair

name: Beetroot / Dietary Nitrate
desc: Dietary nitrate from beetroot is a direct, food-based way to raise nitric oxide — the master vasodilator. Human RCTs consistently show lower blood pressure, better endothelial function, and improved exercise economy (you do more work on less oxygen). One of the cleanest levers for the aging vascular and mitochondrial system. ~400–800 mg nitrate/day.
mechanism: Nitric-oxide production declines with age, and with it goes vascular flexibility and exercise capacity. Beetroot delivers inorganic nitrate that the body converts to nitrite and then NO through a pathway that works *independently* of the age-impaired eNOS enzyme — effectively a back-up NO supply that gets more valuable as you get older. The measured payoffs are lower blood pressure and more efficient muscles.
pathway: A direct, food-based nitric-oxide boost — lower blood pressure and more efficient muscles, backed by consistent RCTs

name: Lion's Mane
desc: Lion's mane (*Hericium erinaceus*) is a culinary mushroom with a genuinely interesting mechanism: its hericenones and erinacines stimulate nerve growth factor (NGF), the signal that keeps neurons healthy and connected. Early human trials point to cognitive and mood benefits; the animal and mechanistic data are strong, the human evidence still emerging. A promising, low-risk cognition play. 500–1,000 mg extract/day.
mechanism: Neuronal maintenance and plasticity fade with age, and NGF — the neurotrophin that supports neuron survival and repair — is central to it. Lion's mane is one of the few natural products shown to raise NGF-related signaling, and that mechanism makes it a compelling candidate for supporting cognition and mood as we age. The upside is meaningful; the honest caveat is that human trials are still small.
pathway: A mushroom that stimulates nerve growth factor — a compelling, low-risk cognition and mood play

name: Citicoline (CDP-Choline)
desc: Citicoline is a highly bioavailable choline source that does double duty: it supplies the raw material for acetylcholine (attention, memory) and for phosphatidylcholine, the phospholipid that builds and repairs neuronal membranes. Human trials show improved attention and memory in healthy adults and support after ischemic injury. A well-tolerated, mechanistically clean cognition tool. 250–500 mg/day.
mechanism: Two things age the brain's signaling: falling acetylcholine tone and degrading neuronal membranes. Citicoline (CDP-choline) feeds both — it is a direct precursor to the neurotransmitter of focus and memory *and* to the phospholipids that keep synaptic membranes intact. That dual role is why it shows up as attention and memory gains in otherwise healthy people, not just in disease.
pathway: Highly bioavailable choline for attention and memory — feeds both acetylcholine and neuronal membrane repair

name: Nattokinase
desc: Nattokinase is a fibrinolytic enzyme purified from natto (fermented soybeans) that directly breaks down fibrin — the protein mesh of blood clots — and supports healthy blood flow. Human RCTs show meaningful reductions in blood pressure and improvements in clot-dissolving activity, with emerging data on arterial plaque. A distinctive, well-tolerated cardiovascular tool. 2,000 FU/day.
mechanism: Blood that clots too readily and flows too thickly is a quiet driver of cardiovascular risk that most supplements never touch. Nattokinase is unusual: it is an actual enzyme with direct fibrinolytic activity — it dissolves fibrin the way the body's own plasmin does — and it also boosts the body's clot-dissolving machinery. That gives it a mechanism no antioxidant or polyphenol has, and it shows up as lower blood pressure and better flow in human trials.
pathway: A fibrinolytic enzyme from natto with human RCTs for blood pressure, clot breakdown, and arterial health

name: MitoQ (Mitoquinol)
desc: MitoQ is CoQ10 re-engineered to actually get *inside* mitochondria — a lipophilic cation drags it hundreds of times more concentrated into the mitochondrial membrane, exactly where age-related oxidative stress does its damage. A landmark human RCT showed it restored vascular function in older adults to that of much younger people. The most targeted mitochondrial antioxidant with real human data. 10–20 mg/day.
mechanism: Ordinary antioxidants mostly wash around the cell and barely reach the mitochondrial inner membrane, where the damage that ages tissues concentrates. MitoQ solves the delivery problem: a triphenylphosphonium tail pulls ubiquinol several-hundred-fold into the mitochondria, letting it neutralize reactive oxygen species at the source. That precision is why it produced a striking human vascular result where generic CoQ10 often does not.
pathway: CoQ10 re-engineered to reach inside mitochondria — a landmark RCT restored older adults' vascular function

name: Aged Garlic Extract
desc: Aged garlic extract is one of the best-evidenced natural cardiovascular supplements: human RCTs show meaningful blood-pressure reduction, and imaging trials show it slows the progression of coronary artery plaque. The aging process converts harsh allicin into stable, bioavailable S-allylcysteine — so it delivers the benefit without the burn or the breath. 600–1,200 mg/day.
mechanism: Blood pressure and arterial plaque are two of the highest-leverage targets in cardiovascular aging, and aged garlic extract (AGE) has real human data on both. Beyond lowering BP, imaging trials show it actually slows coronary calcium and soft-plaque progression — an outcome few supplements can claim. The aging step (up to 20 months) trades unstable allicin for stable, water-soluble S-allylcysteine, giving reliable dosing and none of the GI harshness of raw garlic.
pathway: One of the best-evidenced cardiovascular supplements — lowers blood pressure and slows coronary plaque in imaging trials

name: Metformin
desc: Metformin is a prescription biguanide that inhibits mitochondrial Complex I, lowering cellular energy charge and activating AMPK. Its glucose-lowering and diabetes-prevention data in humans are Tier-A strong (UKPDS 34, DPP). Its geroprotection case is Tier B and genuinely unsettled: it extends lifespan in some mouse models but *not* in the rigorous NIA ITP when given alone, the human TAME longevity trial has not reported, and one RCT shows it can blunt exercise adaptations. This is **not** a native Stack Architect compound — it is a prescription drug and an educational deep-dive only.
mechanism: Metformin is a biguanide, in clinical use for type 2 diabetes for over 60 years. Mechanistically it is a mild mitochondrial poison: it accumulates in cells (aided by OCT1 transporters) and inhibits **Complex I** of the electron transport chain, lowering ATP production and raising the AMP/ATP ratio. That energy-deficit signal activates **AMPK**, the master fuel-sensing kinase, which restrains hepatic gluconeogenesis, promotes fatty-acid oxidation, and — the reason the longevity field cares — pushes cells from a growth-dominant toward a repair-dominant state.
pathway: Metformin → Complex I → AMPK
timingRaw: With meals; ER form at evening meal

name: L-Citrulline
desc: Oral citrulline raises arginine availability and supports nitric-oxide signaling; human evidence focuses on vascular function, blood pressure, and exercise rather than lifespan. Evidence tier: **B**. Use only when the goal and monitoring plan are clear.
mechanism: L-Citrulline is a non-protein amino acid and the most effective *oral* route to raising plasma **arginine** — the substrate the body uses to make **nitric oxide (NO)**. Counterintuitively, swallowing citrulline raises arginine more, and for longer, than swallowing arginine itself: oral arginine is largely destroyed by arginase in the gut wall and liver on first pass, whereas citrulline slips past that first-pass metabolism and is converted to arginine in the kidney. More circulating arginine means more NO available to relax blood vessels — which is why the human evidence clusters around endothelial function, arterial stiffness, blood pressure, and exercise blood flow rather than lifespan.
pathway: Citrulline → arginine → nitric oxide

name: EGCG (Green Tea Catechin)
desc: Epigallocatechin gallate is the dominant catechin in green tea (50–60% of total catechin content) and is unusual among longevity polyphenols for having two distinct, well-characterized mechanistic handles: AMPK activation and direct inhibition of DNA methyltransferase (DNMT). Human RCT data for metabolic markers (blood pressure, LDL, weight) is real but small and inconsistent across meta-analyses. The one genuinely striking human trial — a 90% reduction in prostate cancer incidence in men with precancerous lesions — has not been replicated at scale. The single fact that should govern how you dose this compound: EFSA's 2018 safety review found isolated EGCG doses ≥800 mg/day, especially taken fasted, raise serum liver enzymes, and multiple case reports of acute liver injury exist at doses as low as 140 mg/day in susceptible individuals.
mechanism: AMPK activation: Engages the same cellular energy-deficit signaling as berberine and metformin; suppresses hepatic glucose-6-phosphatase and PEPCK · DNMT1 competitive inhibition: Binds the DNMT catalytic pocket (Ki ≈ 6.9 μM in vitro), reactivating methylation-silenced genes including p16, RARβ, MGMT, and hMLH1 in cancer cell lines · NF-κB / inflammatory suppression: Downregulates COX-2 and inflammatory cytokine transcription in cell and animal models · COMT competition: EGCG is itself a substrate/inhibitor of catechol-O-methyltransferase, the same enzyme that clears catecholamines — a pharmacokinetic detail relevant to interactions, not a benefit
pathway: EGCG → dual AMPK / DNMT mechanism

name: Astaxanthin
desc: Astaxanthin is the deep-red xanthophyll carotenoid from *Haematococcus pluvialis* algae whose polar-nonpolar-polar structure lets it span the lipid bilayer end-to-end, unlike beta-carotene. Human RCTs are genuinely solid for one thing — oral astaxanthin measurably protects skin from UV-induced deterioration and improves elasticity/moisture across a 2021 meta-analysis of 11 controlled studies. Exercise-recovery and oxidative-stress-marker evidence is real but thinner: small trials, mixed endpoints, and one striking 2025 cycling RCT with only 10 subjects. Mitochondrial-biogenesis and lifespan claims are mechanistic and preclinical — no human healthspan trial exists. Tier B.
mechanism: Trans-membrane radical quenching: Polar-nonpolar-polar structure spans the bilayer, neutralizing radicals at both membrane faces · Nrf2 activation / NF-κB suppression: Upregulates antioxidant genes (HO-1, NQO1) while damping inflammatory transcription (Davinelli et al. 2022, PMID 35056816, *Molecules* 27(2):502) · AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α mitochondrial biogenesis: Reported upregulation of PGC-1α, NRF1, TFAM and mitochondrial fusion factors (Mfn1/2, OPA1) in animal and cell-culture models · Immune modulation: Park et al. 2010 (PMID 20205737) found 2–8 mg/day for 8 weeks lowered a DNA-oxidation biomarker and an acute-phase inflammatory protein while enhancing a delayed-hypersensitivity immune response in young healthy women
pathway: Astaxanthin: membrane insertion → dual transcription-factor modulation

name: Apigenin
desc: Apigenin is the flavone behind chamomile's calming reputation, and separately, a 2013 discovery that it inhibits CD38 — the enzyme that consumes NAD+ as we age — in mouse liver and cell culture. Those are two different evidence stories: the sedative/anxiolytic effect has real human RCT support (from whole chamomile extract, not isolated apigenin), while the NAD+-preservation and SASP-suppression story that drives most of the longevity interest is still preclinical. No trial has dosed isolated apigenin in humans and measured NAD+, inflammation, or any aging endpoint. Tier C, and the gap between mouse-liver CD38 data and a human supplement claim is the single most important thing to hold onto here.
mechanism: CD38 inhibition → NAD+ preservation: Blocks the NADase that competes with sirtuins/PARPs for NAD+ · NF-κB / NLRP3 suppression: Blocks IκB kinase and NLRP3 inflammasome assembly, lowering IL-1β release from monocytes/macrophages · SASP suppression: Suppresses IL-1α→IRAK1/IRAK4→p38-MAPK→NF-κB signaling in senescent fibroblasts, cutting CXCL10 (IP-10) secretion · GABA-A benzodiazepine-site binding: Mild anxiolytic/sedative effect
pathway: Apigenin's two mechanistic branches

name: Luteolin
desc: Luteolin is a preclinical anti-inflammatory and senotherapeutic candidate; available human work uses small studies or combination formulations. Evidence tier: **C**. Use only when the goal and monitoring plan are clear.
mechanism: NF-κB inhibition: Suppresses pro-inflammatory gene transcription · Mast-cell stabilization: Reduces histamine/cytokine release · Microglial modulation: Calms CNS immune activation (crosses BBB) · Senotherapeutic signal: Preclinical activity against senescent cells
pathway: Luteolin: anti-inflammatory flavone

name: Ergothioneine
desc: Ergothioneine is a sulfur-containing histidine derivative that only fungi and a few bacteria can synthesize — humans get it entirely from diet (mushrooms are by far the richest source) and evolved a dedicated transporter, OCTN1, just to hoard it in mitochondria-dense tissue. A 21-year Swedish cohort of 3,236 adults found higher plasma ergothioneine predicted lower cardiovascular and all-cause mortality, and dietary ergothioneine extended median lifespan 16% in male mice — but the human interventional record is still thin: a metabolic-syndrome RCT has only published its protocol, and a 16-week cognitive trial showed mixed, mostly secondary-endpoint results. Evidence tier: **C**, anchored by real but non-causal cohort data rather than a positive human RCT on a hard endpoint.
mechanism: Direct ROS/RNS scavenging (thione tautomer): Non-autoxidizing electron donor; quenches •OH, ONOO⁻, HOCl without forming a reactive byproduct · Redox-active metal chelation: Binds Cu²⁺/Fe²⁺, blunting Fenton/Haber-Weiss hydroxyl-radical generation · OCTN1-driven mitochondrial accumulation: Preferentially concentrates in mitochondria of high-turnover, high-oxidative-stress tissue (liver, retina, bone marrow) · Nrf2/NF-κB modulation: Cell and animal studies report antioxidant-gene induction and dampened NF-κB signaling under oxidative challenge (e.g., 7-ketocholesterol-induced endothelial injury models)
pathway: Dietary ERGO → OCTN1 → tissue-specific redox buffering

name: L-Carnosine
desc: L-Carnosine (β-alanyl-L-histidine) scavenges reactive carbonyls that drive advanced glycation end-product (AGE) formation and buffers intracellular pH. The catch that undercuts almost every oral-supplement claim: ingested carnosine is hydrolyzed by serum carnosinase (CN1) with a plasma half-life around 1.2 minutes, so "what you swallow" and "what reaches tissue intact" are not the same thing. Human RCT data is real but narrow — glucose-control trials in prediabetes/T2D are the strongest signal (Tier C overall, closer to B for that one endpoint), autism trials are split between one positive and several null results, and the telomere/senescence story is still cell-culture only.
mechanism: Reactive carbonyl / AGE scavenging: Carnosine's imidazole and free amine form Michael adducts with methylglyoxal and other reactive carbonyls, neutralizing them before they crosslink proteins · Intracellular pH buffering: The imidazole ring (pKa ~6.8) buffers H⁺ generated during anaerobic glycolysis in skeletal muscle · Metal chelation / direct antioxidant: Chelates redox-active copper and zinc, limiting Fenton-type ROS generation · Telomere protection (preclinical): Fu et al. 2004 (PMID 15474517, *Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications*) found cultured normal human fibroblasts grown in 20 mM carnosine showed slower telomere shortening and less telomeric DNA damage across serial passages
pathway: L-Carnosine: two distinct jobs, one absorption problem

name: TMG (Trimethylglycine / Betaine)
desc: Betaine donates methyl groups through BHMT and reliably lowers homocysteine; performance and longevity implications are less certain. Evidence tier: **B**. Use only when the goal and monitoring plan are clear.
mechanism: TMG — trimethylglycine, also called betaine — is a **methyl donor**. Its single best-established job is to hand a methyl group to homocysteine via the enzyme **BHMT (betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase)**, regenerating methionine and reliably lowering blood homocysteine. That makes it a methylation-cycle support compound: relevant to anyone raising homocysteine through high-dose NAD+ precursors (NMN/NR consume methyl groups via NNMT) or with an MTHFR variant. It is also an osmolyte the kidney and liver use for cell-volume regulation. The performance and longevity claims are weaker than the homocysteine effect — hold them to a higher bar.
pathway: Betaine → methylation cycle

name: Tocotrienols (Vitamin E)
desc: Tocotrienols are vitamin-E isoforms distinct from alpha-tocopherol, with human trials in lipids and metabolic or liver endpoints but no direct lifespan evidence. Evidence tier: **B**. Use only when the goal and monitoring plan are clear.
mechanism: Lipid-phase antioxidant: Quenches membrane/lipoprotein peroxidation · HMG-CoA reductase suppression: δ/γ isoforms lower LDL cholesterol · NF-κB downregulation: Reduces inflammatory signaling · Isoform/absorption caveat: α-tocopherol competes for uptake
pathway: Tocotrienols: membrane redox + lipid control

name: Butyrate (Sodium / Tributyrin)
desc: Butyrate is the short-chain fatty acid your own colonic bacteria make when you eat fermentable fiber — it's the primary fuel for colonocytes and a genuine HDAC inhibitor. Oral supplementation (microencapsulated sodium butyrate or tributyrin) has real human RCT support, but almost entirely in disease populations — IBS, diverticulosis, ulcerative colitis, type 2 diabetes — at doses of 300 mg to 1.5 g/day. The largest and most rigorous trial to date (n=181, MASLD) missed its primary liver-fat endpoint. No trial has tested it in healthy adults for a longevity outcome. Evidence tier: **B**, honestly disease-population evidence, not a settled healthy-adult intervention.
mechanism: HDAC inhibition (Class I/IIa): Hyperacetylates histone H3/H4, de-repressing anti-inflammatory and barrier-gene transcription · GPR109A (HCAR2) activation: Anti-inflammatory signaling in colonic macrophages and Tregs; the receptor tributyrin acts through in adipose tissue (Sato et al. 2020, PMID 32882837) · GPR41 (FFAR3) activation: Enteroendocrine signaling linked to satiety hormones and glucose homeostasis · Colonocyte β-oxidation: Primary ATP substrate for the colonic epithelium — normal colonocytes burn it for fuel, while cancerous colonocytes (glycolytic, "Warburg" phenotype) accumulate it and are instead growth-arrested by its HDAC-inhibiting action
pathway: Butyrate → HDAC inhibition + GPR41/109A → barrier and metabolic effects
dose: 300 mg–1.5 g/day microencapsulated sodium butyrate, or 200–400 mg/day tributyrin

name: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera)
desc: Ashwagandha root extract is the best-evidenced adaptogen for perceived stress, anxiety symptoms, and self-reported sleep quality, anchored by a 60-day RCT showing a 27.9% serum-cortisol drop and a 2022 meta-analysis of 12 RCTs (n=1,002) confirming the anxiety/stress effect. A separate 8-week RCT also found real strength and testosterone gains in resistance-trained men. The genuine caution: a growing case-series literature (Iceland/US DILIN, five patients) documents idiosyncratic cholestatic liver injury, almost always self-limited but occasionally severe — this is not a "no downside" botanical.
mechanism: GABA-mimetic / GABA-A modulation: Withanolides (withanolide A, withaferin A) bind GABA-A receptor sites, producing anxiolytic-like effects in preclinical models · HPA-axis dampening: Blunts the cortisol surge to acute and chronic stressors, the best human-validated mechanism · NF-κB / cytokine suppression: Withaferin A inhibits NF-κB signaling in vitro, reducing downstream inflammatory cytokines · Androgen/anabolic signaling: Resistance-training RCT found significant testosterone increases alongside strength gains — mechanism not fully isolated from stress-hormone reduction
pathway: Withanolides → HPA-axis dampening → stress/sleep outcomes
dose: 300 mg BID (600 mg/day) standardized root extract, ≥5% withanolides
timingRaw: AM/PM split for stress dosing; PM for sleep-only use

name: Rhodiola rosea
desc: Rhodiola has modest human evidence for fatigue and stress, but study quality varies and lifespan findings are preclinical. Evidence tier: **C**. Use only when the goal and monitoring plan are clear.
mechanism: Rhodiola rosea is an **adaptogen** — a plant extract studied for blunting the physiological cost of stress and fatigue. Its activity is attributed to two marker compounds, **rosavins** and **salidroside** (quality extracts are standardized to ~3% rosavins / ~1% salidroside, the "SHR-5" ratio used in most trials). The best human signal is for stress-related fatigue and mental performance under load; the lifespan findings are preclinical (fruit fly, worm, and rodent models). Treat it as a stress/fatigue support compound, not a longevity intervention.
pathway: Rhodiola: adaptogenic stress modulation

name: Nicotinamide (NAM)
desc: Nicotinamide is a non-flushing vitamin-B3 form with strong evidence for reducing new non-melanoma skin cancers in high-risk patients; high doses are not interchangeable with general NAD support. Evidence tier: **B**. Use only when the goal and monitoring plan are clear.
mechanism: Nicotinamide (NAM) is the **amide form of vitamin B3** and a direct entry point to the NAD+ salvage pathway — but it behaves very differently from NMN/NR and from flushing niacin (nicotinic acid). Unlike niacin, it does **not** cause the skin flush and does **not** lower cholesterol; unlike NMN/NR, its standout human evidence is not "general NAD+ boosting" but a specific dermatology result: oral nicotinamide reduces the rate of new non-melanoma skin cancers and actinic keratoses in high-risk patients. The critical nuance is dose duality — nicotinamide *feeds* NAD+ synthesis, yet at high concentrations it can *inhibit* the very NAD+-consuming enzymes (sirtuins, PARPs) that NAD+ is meant to fuel.
pathway: Nicotinamide → NAD+ salvage
dose: 500 mg twice daily for indicated skin protocol

name: Hesperidin
desc: Hesperidin is the citrus flavanone glycoside behind orange juice's vascular effects. Small mechanistic RCTs are genuinely encouraging — a 2011 crossover trial found it restores nitric-oxide-dependent endothelial function in metabolic syndrome, and a 159-person 2021 trial found hesperidin-enriched orange juice lowered systolic and pulse pressure in mild hypertension over 12 weeks. But the largest pooled analysis (10 RCTs, n=577) found no significant effect on lipids or blood pressure, and a 2016 trial in overweight adults found no FMD improvement except in a post-hoc subgroup. Absorption is the other catch: hesperidin's rutinose sugar blocks small-intestinal uptake, so most of what you swallow depends on your colonic bacteria to convert it before it can do anything.
mechanism: Colonic bio-activation: Gut bacterial α-rhamnosidase hydrolyzes the rutinose sugar to release absorbable hesperetin · eNOS/NO signaling: Hesperetin stimulates Src, Akt, AMPK, and eNOS phosphorylation in endothelial cells, requiring H2O2 as a signaling intermediate (Rizza 2011 in-vitro arm) · Adhesion molecule suppression: Reduces soluble VCAM-1/ICAM-1 in responders, lowering leukocyte–endothelium adhesion · Gene-expression modulation: CITRUS study found hesperidin-enriched OJ changed expression of PTX3, NLRP3, NPSR1, and NAMPT in blood cells after 12 weeks
pathway: Hesperidin → colonic hydrolysis → eNOS/NO → vascular readout

name: Boswellia serrata (AKBA)
desc: Boswellia serrata gum resin, standardized to its most potent constituent (AKBA, 3-O-acetyl-11-keto-β-boswellic acid), is a genuine 5-lipoxygenase inhibitor with real human RCT support for knee osteoarthritis pain and function — a 2020 meta-analysis of 7 trials (n=545) found a 14-point WOMAC pain reduction. The catch: nearly every positive human trial was funded by, and its authors affiliated with, the manufacturer of the extract tested (5-Loxin®/Aflapin®), and a 2025 mechanistic paper found a *low*-AKBA extract outperformed a high-AKBA one — complicating the "more AKBA is better" premise the whole category is marketed on. Oral AKBA absorption is also extremely poor (well under 2%). Tier B: real, repeatable OA relief, read with appropriate skepticism about who ran the trials.
mechanism: 5-LOX inhibition: AKBA binds 5-LOX at a non-catalytic, non-redox regulatory site, distinct from how most 5-LOX drugs work (Sailer et al. 1996, PMID 8646405) · Leukotriene reduction: Downstream drop in LTB4 and related mediators that drive neutrophil chemotaxis and joint swelling · Cartilage matrix protection: Sengupta 2008 measured reduced urinary MMP-3 (a cartilage-degrading enzyme) alongside symptom improvement · "Lipid mediator class switch": Nischang et al. 2025 (PMID 41075523) found low-AKBA extracts can outperform high-AKBA ones on pro-resolving mediator shifts, implying the active fraction is broader than AKBA alone
pathway: AKBA → 5-LOX blockade → fewer leukotrienes
timingRaw: With food, split AM/PM if using higher doses

name: Gynostemma pentaphyllum (Jiaogulan)
desc: Gynostemma pentaphyllum ("Jiaogulan," the Southern Chinese "herb of immortality") contains gypenosides — dammarane-type saponins structurally related to ginsenosides — that, once heat-processed into damulins A and B, directly activate AMPK. Three small human RCTs, all at the same 450 mg/day dose, report real body-composition, lipid, and exercise-performance effects. The catch: all three are funded by the extract's manufacturer, none is independently replicated at scale, and the AMPK story — while mechanistically real — has not been tested against a hard longevity endpoint. Tier C: a legitimate, cheap AMPK-activator candidate, not a settled metabolic intervention.
mechanism: Heat-processing → damulin A/B: Autoclaving converts native gypenosides into damulins A and B, the fraction identified as the AMPK-activating compounds (PMID 22576281) · AMPK-α Thr172 phosphorylation: Damulins increase AMPK-α phosphorylation in L6 myotubes and in ob/ob mouse soleus muscle; confirmed in human muscle biopsies post-exercise (PMID 38004115) · ACC inhibition / substrate switching: AMPK activation suppresses acetyl-CoA carboxylase, shifting muscle toward fat oxidation over lipogenesis — the same downstream node berberine and metformin converge on
pathway: Gypenosides → damulins → AMPK → fat oxidation

name: Low-Dose Lithium
desc: Ecological and preclinical signals are hypothesis-generating only; even low exposure can affect thyroid and kidney function, and lithium orotate lacks robust longevity trials. Evidence tier: **C**. Use only when the goal and monitoring plan are clear.
mechanism: GSK-3β inhibition: Primary target; enables the effects below · Autophagy induction: Clears aggregated proteins · ↓ Tau phosphorylation: Reduces a driver of neurodegeneration · Neurotrophic/circadian tone: BDNF and rhythm modulation
pathway: Low-dose lithium: GSK-3β inhibition

name: Hyaluronic Acid (Oral)
desc: Oral hyaluronic acid (sodium hyaluronate, typically ~1–2 MDa, dosed 100–240 mg/day) has real, repeated placebo-controlled RCT evidence for skin hydration and wrinkle depth — a 2025 meta-analysis of 7 trials confirms it — plus a smaller signal for knee osteoarthritis symptoms. The catch: intact HA is a giant polysaccharide that shouldn't survive the gut, so oral efficacy depends on a mechanism that's still being worked out — gut-microbiota fragmentation into small oligosaccharides, with only ~0.2% net bioavailability. This is skin/joint-symptom evidence, not longevity evidence.
mechanism: Microbial fragmentation: *Bacteroides* and other gut species cleave ingested HA into oligosaccharides <3 kDa (PMID 18959406 tracer studies; in vitro fermentation studies) · Epithelial/lymphatic uptake: Small fragments cross the gut wall and transfer via lymph to systemic circulation · CD44/TLR receptor engagement: HA fragments are proposed ligands for CD44 and TLR2/TLR4 on fibroblasts and synoviocytes, potentially triggering local HA synthase upregulation · SCFA byproduct: The majority of ingested HA that is *not* absorbed is fermented to acetate/propionate/butyrate, with secondary effects on gut microbial composition
pathway: Oral HA → gut fermentation → connective-tissue signaling

name: Inulin / Prebiotic Fiber
desc: Inulin is a chicory-root fructan that human digestive enzymes cannot break down, so it travels intact to the colon where *Bifidobacterium* and butyrate-producing species ferment it into short-chain fatty acids. A 33-trial, GRADE-assessed dose-response meta-analysis (n=1,346) found real reductions in fasting glucose and HbA1c in prediabetes/T2D at ≥10 g/day for 6+ weeks — but a crossover trial of the same fermentation pathway found no effect on appetite hormones, and a head-to-head trial found plain inulin didn't move systemic inflammatory markers the way its propionate-ester derivative did. Tier B: real, repeatable fermentation biology with genuine glycemic and bowel-regularity evidence, honestly short of a clean anti-inflammatory or satiety story.
mechanism: Selective bifidogenic shift: Increases *Bifidobacterium* abundance more consistently than any other taxon change · SCFA production (acetate/propionate/butyrate): Colonic fermentation yields measurable, quantifiable SCFA output · Incretin signaling (GLP-1/PYY): SCFAs stimulate L-cell incretin release via GPR41/43 — theoretically appetite-relevant · Propionate-mediated insulin sensitization: Propionate specifically improves peripheral insulin sensitivity, distinct from butyrate's colonocyte role
pathway: Inulin → colonic fermentation → SCFA signaling
timingRaw: With meals, split across the day at higher doses

name: Acarbose
desc: Acarbose extends mouse lifespan in the NIA Intervention Testing Program and improves postprandial glucose in humans, but healthy-human longevity benefit is unproven and gastrointestinal effects are common. Evidence tier: **B**. This is an educational research module—not a self-treatment recommendation.
mechanism: α-glucosidase inhibition: Slows carb→glucose digestion · Lower postprandial glucose/insulin: Flatter glycemic curve · Colonic SCFA production: Fermentation → butyrate · Reduced glycation/inflammaging: Fewer glucose excursions
pathway: Acarbose: post-meal glucose attenuation
timingRaw: with the first bite of meals

name: Canagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor)
desc: SGLT2 inhibition has strong cardiorenal outcome data in indicated patients and male-mouse lifespan data, but it is not a healthy-person longevity supplement and carries ketoacidosis and infection risks. Evidence tier: **B**. This is an educational research module—not a self-treatment recommendation.
mechanism: Renal SGLT2 inhibition: Blocks glucose reabsorption → glucosuria · Insulin-independent glucose lowering: Reduces glucotoxicity · Ketone/metabolic shift: Mild deficit, substrate switch · Cardiorenal protection: Hemodynamic/energetic effects
pathway: Canagliflozin: renal glucose excretion

name: Dasatinib
desc: Dasatinib plus quercetin has early human senolytic studies, but dasatinib is a potent leukemia drug with serious hematologic and infectious risks and no role in self-experimentation. Evidence tier: **C**. This is an educational research module—not a self-treatment recommendation.
mechanism: SFK/ephrin kinase inhibition: Disables senescent-cell survival signaling · Senolytic apoptosis: Selective death of senescent cells · Pulsed dosing: Intermittent hit-and-run, not daily · SASP reduction: Fewer inflammatory secretions after clearance
pathway: Dasatinib: senolysis via kinase inhibition

name: Alpha-GPC (L-Alpha-Glycerylphosphorylcholine)
desc: Alpha-GPC is the most bioavailable choline delivery form, crossing the blood–brain barrier and raising synaptic acetylcholine. Tier B human evidence for cognitive support in mild-to-moderate cognitive impairment (ASCOMALVA, De Jesus Moreno 2003) and acute focus/reaction time in adults. Standard dose 300–600 mg/day; take with food; avoid stacking with other choline sources unless targeting >1,200 mg/day total.
mechanism: Choline delivery: Hydrolyzed to glycerophosphate + choline; ~40% brain bioavailability · Acetylcholine synthesis: Presynaptic ChAT uses free choline + acetyl-CoA → ACh · Membrane phosphatidylcholine: Choline + CTP → CDP-choline → PC (Kennedy pathway) · Growth hormone (acute): Cholinergic stimulation of pituitary → transient GH pulse
pathway: The choline form that reaches the brain — cholinergic support with real cognitive-decline RCTs
timingRaw: AM with food; pre-workout for acute performance

name: Phosphatidylserine (PS)
desc: Phosphatidylserine is a membrane phospholipid essential to neuronal signaling. Human trials show cognitive support in aging (Crook 1991, PMID 1876787) and cortisol dampening after exercise stress (Starks 2008, PMID 18662395). Modern soy-derived PS at 100–300 mg/day is safe and well-tolerated; the older bovine-cortex PS with the classic dementia trials is no longer available.
mechanism: Membrane composition: Restores PS in aging neuronal membranes · Synaptic signaling: Anchors PKC, activates Raf-1 → MAPK cascade · ACTH/cortisol: Dampens ACTH release; blunts cortisol response to physical stress · Apoptotic flag: PS externalization marks cells for phagocytosis (this is regulated, not disrupted by supplementation)
pathway: Neuronal membrane phospholipid — cognitive support and the reproducible post-exercise cortisol lever

name: Ginkgo Biloba (EGb 761)
desc: Ginkgo biloba standardized extract (EGb 761: 24% flavone glycosides, 6% terpene lactones) is a vasodilator + antioxidant with real, large RCT evidence for cognitive function in dementia (Le Bars 1997, PMID 9343463) and mixed evidence for prevention in healthy adults (GEM trial 2008, PMID 18544724 — negative for AD prevention). Standard dose 120–240 mg/day EGb 761; expect signal at 12+ weeks; discontinue 2 weeks before surgery due to platelet effects.
mechanism: PAF antagonism: Ginkgolide B binds PAF receptor → ↓ platelet aggregation · Cerebral blood flow: Vasodilation via NO + endothelial function · Mitochondrial protection: Bilobalide preserves Complex I/III in ischemia · Antioxidant: Flavone glycosides quench ROS · MAO-B inhibition: Mild, contributes to dopaminergic effects
pathway: Vascular cognition — real effect in established dementia, negative for prevention (GEM trial)

name: Panax Ginseng (Korean / Asian Ginseng)
desc: Panax ginseng root standardized to 4–8% total ginsenosides is an adaptogen with human RCT evidence for fatigue reduction in chronic illness (Barton 2013, PMID 23853036 — cancer-related fatigue), modest cognitive support in MCI, and improved glycemic control in type 2 diabetes. Standard dose 200–400 mg/day standardized extract or 1–2 g/day root powder. Distinguished from American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius) which is more "cooling" per TCM.
mechanism: HPA modulation: Rg1 dampens cortisol response to stress · Glycemic: AMPK activation → improved insulin sensitivity + ↓ postprandial glucose · Endothelial NO: Rg1 activates eNOS → vasodilation · Cognitive: Rb1 modulates cholinergic + GABAergic tone · Anti-inflammatory: Suppresses NF-κB in immune cells
pathway: Adaptogen with real fatigue-reduction and glycemic RCTs — cycle to prevent tachyphylaxis

name: Mucuna Pruriens (Velvet Bean, L-DOPA)
desc: Mucuna pruriens seed contains 3.6–6% natural L-DOPA — the direct dopamine precursor. RCTs in Parkinson's show it works comparably to synthetic levodopa with somewhat lower dyskinesia burden (Katzenschlager 2004, PMID 15489397). Standardized to 15% L-DOPA at 100–500 mg/day for wellness use; **not a self-treatment for Parkinson's** — that's Rx-managed. Contains L-DOPA which is a real drug; treat this as pharmaceutical-grade caution.
mechanism: Dopamine synthesis: L-DOPA → dopamine via AADC in surviving neurons · Prolactin suppression: Dopamine inhibits pituitary prolactin release · Antioxidant: Seed extract has GSH-preserving effects in preclinical PD · Anti-inflammatory: Alkaloids reduce microglial activation preclinically
pathway: Natural L-DOPA — dopaminergic support that should be treated as a real drug, not just an herb
dose: 100–300 mg/day of 15% L-DOPA extract (= 15–45 mg L-DOPA)

name: Theobromine
desc: Theobromine is the primary methylxanthine in cocoa (~2% of raw cocoa mass), a mild vasodilator and cough suppressant with real cardiovascular signal from cocoa RCTs but thin evidence for isolated supplementation. Standard exposure: 200–400 mg/day via 20–40 g of ≥85% dark chocolate. Not stimulating like caffeine — smoother, longer half-life (~7h vs 5h). Extreme toxicity in dogs — never allow pets access.
mechanism: Adenosine A2A antagonism: Vasodilation in peripheral vessels · PDE inhibition: ↑ cAMP → smooth muscle relaxation · Cough suppression: Central vagal afferent modulation · Blood pressure: Small ↓ SBP in short-term human studies · HDL modulation: Small ↑ HDL-C in cocoa trials (mechanism uncertain)
pathway: Cocoa's cardiovascular fraction — vasodilator, cough suppressant, and 7-hour half-life

name: Capsaicin (Cayenne / Chili)
desc: Capsaicin, the pungent alkaloid in chili peppers, is a TRPV1 agonist with real evidence for metabolic health, satiety, and a mortality signal: China Kadoorie Biobank (~500k adults) found 6–7 chili meals per week associated with **14% lower all-cause mortality** (Lv 2015, PMID 26232331). Dietary use via chili peppers is the primary evidence route; supplemental capsaicin 2–6 mg/day is well tolerated but topical (0.025–0.075% cream) is where the RCT evidence for pain is strongest.
mechanism: TRPV1 activation: Depolarizes sensory neurons + BAT/gut cells · Thermogenesis: Sympathetic activation of brown adipose · Satiety: Gut TRPV1 → ↑ GLP-1, PYY release · Anti-inflammatory: Suppresses NF-κB in adipose tissue · Mitochondrial biogenesis: TRPV1 → PGC-1α upregulation · Endothelial function: Improves NO-mediated vasodilation
pathway: TRPV1 agonist with a 14% mortality signal in China Kadoorie and topical Tier A for neuropathic pain

name: Pumpkin Seed Oil
desc: Pumpkin seed oil (from Cucurbita pepo) is a lignan-rich oil with real RCT evidence for benign prostatic hyperplasia symptom relief (Vahlensieck 2015, PMID 25874948 — GRANU study) and androgen alopecia in men (Cho 2014, PMID 24864154). Standard dose: 1,000 mg/day soft-gels or 1–2 tbsp cold-pressed oil. Contains phytosterols (β-sitosterol) plus lignans (secoisolariciresinol) — weak 5α-reductase modulation is the leading hypothesis.
mechanism: 5α-reductase: Weak inhibition by phytosterols + lignans (weaker than finasteride) · Anti-inflammatory (prostate): Reduces prostatic COX-2 and IL-6 preclinically · Antioxidant: Vitamin E + carotenoids · Bladder smooth muscle: Direct calming effect on detrusor overactivity · Zinc supply: 100 g seeds ≈ 10 mg zinc (RDA is 11 mg for men)
pathway: Weak 5α-reductase modulator with the GRANU BPH trial and a real male-AGA hair-count signal
dose: 1,000 mg/day standardized extract OR 1–2 tbsp cold-pressed oil

name: Superoxide Dismutase (SOD, Oral GliSODin)
desc: Superoxide dismutase (SOD) is the primary intracellular antioxidant enzyme neutralizing O₂⁻ to H₂O₂. As a supplement, GliSODin (French melon SOD + gliadin coating for GI protection) has small human RCT signals for skin (UV protection), exercise recovery, and oxidative stress markers. Standard dose 250–500 mg/day. **Not** a replacement for the endogenous SOD your cells make — the ingested enzyme is degraded; effect appears to be a "signaling" response that induces endogenous antioxidant genes.
mechanism: Nrf2 induction: Gut lymphoid uptake → systemic Nrf2/ARE activation · Endogenous antioxidant upregulation: ↑ SOD, catalase, GPx expression · Cytokine modulation: ↓ IL-6, TNF-α in inflammatory states · Direct enzyme delivery: Likely minimal — most SOD is digested
pathway: Melon-derived SOD with gliadin coating — an Nrf2 signaling dose, not an enzyme-replacement supplement

name: Piperine (BioPerine)
desc: Piperine is the pungent alkaloid in black pepper (~5–9% of Piper nigrum by weight). Its role in longevity supplementation is as a **bioenhancer**: piperine inhibits intestinal glucuronidation and P-glycoprotein efflux, dramatically increasing systemic exposure to curcumin (2,000% — Shoba 1998, PMID 9619120), resveratrol, EGCG, and CoQ10. Standard dose 5–20 mg piperine per compound dose. Direct-effect evidence is thinner; the RCT evidence is almost entirely about enhancing what it's paired with.
mechanism: UGT inhibition: Blocks intestinal + hepatic glucuronidation · P-glycoprotein inhibition: Reduces intestinal efflux of substrates · CYP3A4 modulation: Modest inhibition · Tight junction modulation: Increases mucosal permeability
pathway: Black-pepper bioenhancer — 20× curcumin absorption, and a real drug-interaction concern
dose: 5–20 mg piperine with each compound dose

name: MCT Oil (Medium-Chain Triglycerides / C8:C10)
desc: MCT oil (medium-chain triglycerides, primarily caprylic C8:0 and capric C10:0) is absorbed via the portal vein without micelle formation, delivered directly to hepatocytes, and rapidly β-oxidized to ketones. Human RCTs show ketone elevation (Vandenberghe 2017), improved cognition in mild AD (Cunnane 2020), and modest weight-management effects. Standard dose 10–30 g/day (start low: GI upset is dose-limiting). C8-only ("caprylic") produces the highest ketone response per gram.
mechanism: Portal vein absorption: Bypass chylomicron pathway → direct liver uptake · Hepatic β-oxidation: Rapid oxidation → acetyl-CoA + NADH · Ketogenesis: Excess acetyl-CoA → acetoacetate + β-hydroxybutyrate · Brain ketone uptake: MCT1/2 transporters unchanged with age; provides alternative fuel · Mitochondrial biogenesis: β-hydroxybutyrate signals via HCAR2, HDAC inhibition
pathway: Portal-vein absorbed fats → ketones → the Cunnane MCI cognitive brain-fuel intervention
timingRaw: AM or pre-fast for ketone bridge

name: Bacopa Monnieri (Brahmi)
desc: Bacopa monnieri is an Ayurvedic nootropic with real RCT evidence for memory consolidation in healthy adults (Stough 2001 PMID 11498727; Morgan 2010 PMID 20590480) and mild cognitive support in older adults. The active bacosides work slowly — effects appear at 8–12 weeks of consistent dosing, not acutely. Standard dose 300 mg/day of 50% bacoside-standardized extract (or 750 mg/day of 20%). GI upset common; take with food.
mechanism: Cholinergic: Bacosides increase ACh availability, weak AChE inhibition · Serotonergic: 5-HT increased in hippocampus (preclinical); antidepressant-like · Antioxidant: ↑ SOD, catalase, GPx in brain tissue · Dendritic branching: ↑ Hippocampal CA1 dendritic length (Vollala rat model) · Anti-inflammatory: ↓ TNF-α, IL-6 in microglia
pathway: Ayurvedic nootropic — real memory consolidation at 8-12 weeks, no acute effect

name: Cordyceps (Cordyceps militaris / sinensis)
desc: Cordyceps is a medicinal mushroom with real preclinical mitochondrial-biogenesis mechanisms (via cordycepin and adenosine) but only modest human RCT evidence for VO₂max and exercise economy (Chen 2010 PMID 20804807 — small older-adult trial). Cultivated C. militaris fruiting body (higher cordycepin) is the practical form; C. sinensis wild-harvested is expensive and often adulterated. Standard dose 1–3 g/day extract; cycle 6 weeks on / 1 week off.
mechanism: Cordycepin / adenosine: Modulates AMPK, mTOR; anti-proliferative in cancer models · Mitochondrial biogenesis: PGC-1α upregulation preclinically · Immunomodulation: β-glucans activate dendritic cells + NK cells · Anti-inflammatory: ↓ NF-κB, ↓ TNF-α in mouse models · Erythropoiesis: Traditional use for anemia; small human signal
pathway: Medicinal mushroom with a plausible mitochondrial mechanism and one honest older-adult VO₂max RCT

name: Reishi (Ganoderma lucidum)
desc: Reishi (Ganoderma lucidum) is the classical "spirit mushroom" of TCM. Human RCTs show immunomodulation via β-glucans (mixed cancer-adjunct data), small sleep-quality signal, and cardiovascular/glycemic biomarker changes. Larger meta-analyses find effect sizes small and inconsistent. Standard dose 1.5–3 g/day dual-extract (hot water + alcohol) to capture both β-glucans and triterpenoids. Real drug-interaction risks with anticoagulants and immunosuppressants.
mechanism: Dectin-1 / TLR2: β-glucans activate innate immunity · NK cell activity: Increased in cancer-adjunct trials · HMG-CoA reductase inhibition: Triterpenoids (weak, statin-like) · NF-κB modulation: Reduced inflammatory cytokines preclinically · GABAergic (proposed): Sleep effect hypothesis; mechanism unclear
pathway: "Spirit mushroom" of TCM — genuine immune mechanism, modest human evidence
timingRaw: Evening if targeting sleep; anytime otherwise

name: Turkey Tail (Trametes versicolor, PSK / PSP)
desc: Turkey tail is the best-evidenced medicinal mushroom on this list. Its polysaccharide extracts **PSK (Krestin)** and **PSP** are approved cancer-adjunct therapies in Japan and China, with meta-analytic survival benefit in gastric and colorectal cancer when added to standard chemotherapy (Oba 2007, PMID 17351811 — gastric cancer 5-year survival OR 0.71). Standard supplement dose 2–3 g/day dual-extract. Wellness/immune-support use is far less evidenced than the cancer-adjunct data.
mechanism: Dectin-1 activation: β-glucan → macrophage TNF-α, IL-6 signaling · NK cell activity: Consistently ↑ in cancer-adjunct trials · Antigen presentation: ↑ Dendritic cell maturation · T-cell modulation: ↑ Th1 response; ↓ Treg burden · Tumor microenvironment: ↓ Tumor-associated macrophage M2 polarization
pathway: The best-evidenced medicinal mushroom — PSK is an approved oncology adjunct in Japan and China

name: Astragalus (Astragalus membranaceus)
desc: Astragalus root is a classical TCM immune tonic. The longevity backstory is the cycloastragenol / astragaloside IV → TA-65 telomerase-activator lineage (Bernardes de Jesus 2011 mouse data; small human safety trials of TA-65). Meaningful human RCTs of Astragalus itself are for cancer-adjunct chemotherapy tolerability and modest cardiovascular biomarker effects. Standard dose 2–4 g/day extract or 500–1,000 mg standardized astragaloside IV. Real interactions with immunosuppressants.
mechanism: Telomerase activation: Astragaloside IV / cycloastragenol → hTERT expression (small effect in humans) · Immune modulation: APS activate macrophages, NK cells · Anti-inflammatory: Suppresses TNF-α, IL-6, NF-κB preclinically · Cardiovascular: Modest ↓ BP, ↑ endothelial NO in RCTs · Renal protection: Slows CKD progression in some RCTs (diabetic nephropathy)
pathway: The cycloastragenol / TA-65 telomere story — real, modest, and expensive

name: Milk Thistle (Silymarin / Silybin)
desc: Milk thistle standardized to 70–80% silymarin (a flavonolignan complex — silybin A/B, silydianin, silychristin) has real human RCT evidence for **non-alcoholic fatty liver disease** (Loguercio 2012, PMID 22240442), **type 2 diabetes glycemic control** (Huseini 2006, PMID 17094080), and modest chemoprotection during hepatotoxic drug therapy. Standard dose 420–600 mg silymarin/day divided TID. Silybin phytosome (Siliphos, Legalon) has ~10× better bioavailability than plain silymarin extract.
mechanism: Antioxidant (hepatic): Preserves hepatic GSH; scavenges lipid peroxidation radicals · Membrane stabilization: Competes for OATP1B3 uptake with hepatotoxins · Anti-fibrotic: Inhibits TGF-β → stellate cell activation · Insulin sensitivity: Reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis; improves peripheral insulin action · PON1 activity: Increases paraoxonase 1 (anti-atherogenic enzyme)
pathway: Flavonolignan hepatoprotection — real NAFLD and diabetic-glycemic RCT evidence

name: MSM (Methylsulfonylmethane)
desc: MSM is an organosulfur compound (dimethyl sulfone) that supplies bioavailable sulfur for collagen and glutathione synthesis. Two RCTs show modest knee osteoarthritis pain reduction at 1.5–6 g/day (Kim 2006 PMID 16309928; Debbi 2011 PMID 21708034). Also small skin/hair benefits and post-exercise recovery signals. Well tolerated at 1–6 g/day; the sulfur odor complaints are mostly urea/skin, not from MSM itself.
mechanism: Sulfur donation: Contributes to cysteine/methionine cycles · GSH substrate: Provides sulfur for glutathione biosynthesis · Collagen synthesis: Sulfur required for hydroxyproline crosslinks · Anti-inflammatory: Suppresses NF-κB, MAPK in cartilage cells preclinically · Antioxidant: Direct radical scavenging (weak); GSH-mediated (strong)
pathway: Bioavailable sulfur for connective tissue and GSH substrate — modest knee-OA RCT signal

name: Chondroitin Sulfate
desc: Chondroitin sulfate is a glycosaminoglycan structural component of cartilage. Meta-analyses of osteoarthritis RCTs show modest pain reduction and slowed cartilage loss (Fransen 2015 PMID 25574023; MOVES trial 2016 PMID 26686842). Standard dose 800–1,200 mg/day, usually paired with glucosamine (1,500 mg). Effect size is small (~10% pain reduction vs placebo); it's a maintenance intervention, not acute pain relief. Bovine-cartilage source dominant; pharmaceutical-grade (Bioiberica, Chondrosulf) preferred.
mechanism: Cartilage substrate: Provides GAG monomers for aggrecan resynthesis · Anti-catabolic: Inhibits ADAMTS-4/5 and MMP-3/13 (cartilage-degrading enzymes) · Chondrocyte anabolic: Increases proteoglycan synthesis in chondrocytes · Anti-inflammatory: Reduces synovial NF-κB and IL-1β signaling · Sulfate donor: Contributes to overall body sulfate pool
pathway: Cartilage glycosaminoglycan — MOVES showed non-inferiority to celecoxib for knee OA

name: UC-II (Undenatured Type II Collagen)
desc: UC-II is native (undenatured) type II collagen sourced from chicken sternum, dosed at just **40 mg/day** — orders of magnitude smaller than hydrolyzed collagen peptides. The mechanism is **oral tolerance immunomodulation** (Peyer's patches → reduced auto-reactive T-cell response to joint collagen), not amino acid substrate. Two well-designed RCTs (Lugo 2016 PMID 27614638; Crowley 2009 PMID 19856234) show UC-II outperforms glucosamine + chondroitin for knee osteoarthritis symptoms. Distinct from collagen peptides — do not confuse.
mechanism: Peyer's patch antigen presentation: Native TII collagen presented to gut lymphoid tissue · Regulatory T-cell induction: Anti-inflammatory Tregs proliferate in response · Systemic tolerance: Tregs migrate to joints, reduce cartilage inflammation · Reduced pro-inflammatory cytokines: ↓ IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α in synovium · Cartilage protection: Preservation of aggrecan, type II collagen matrix
pathway: Native chicken-sternum collagen at 40 mg/day — oral tolerance, not substrate; beats G+C in head-to-head RCTs
dose: 40 mg once daily on empty stomach

name: Bromelain
desc: Bromelain is a mixture of proteolytic enzymes from pineapple stem and fruit. Real RCT evidence for post-surgical / post-injury edema and pain reduction (Kerkhoffs 2004 PMID 15150435 — ankle sprain), acute sinusitis symptom relief (Guo 2018 PMID 30319719 meta), and adjunct osteoarthritis pain. Standard dose 500–2,000 mg/day (2,400 GDU/g) between meals; with meals reduces protein digestion. Well tolerated. Real anticoagulant potentiation to know about.
mechanism: Fibrinolysis: Direct enzymatic degradation of fibrin · Bradykinin degradation: Reduces inflammatory kinin pool · Anti-edema: Improves lymphatic drainage of exudate · Prostaglandin modulation: Small effect via arachidonic acid pathway · Immune modulation: ↓ CD44 shedding; alters leukocyte trafficking
pathway: Pineapple proteolytic enzyme — sports medicine and sinusitis workhorse, real anticoagulant potentiation

name: Methylfolate (L-5-MTHF / L-Methylfolate)
desc: L-5-methyltetrahydrofolate is the bioactive folate form that bypasses the MTHFR enzyme bottleneck (677C>T variants slow methylation of folic acid ~30–70%). Human RCT evidence for depression augmentation (Papakostas 2012 PMID 22945484), homocysteine lowering, and neural-tube defect prevention. Standard dose 400–1,000 mcg/day (over-the-counter); depression trials use 15 mg/day (Rx-controlled Deplin). If you have MTHFR variants, use methylfolate — not synthetic folic acid.
mechanism: MTHFR bypass: Skips the enzymatic bottleneck · Homocysteine remethylation: 5-MTHF donates methyl to Hcy → methionine · SAM production: Methionine → SAM → DNA/histone methylation · Neurotransmitter synthesis: BH4 cofactor stability → dopamine, serotonin, norepinephrine synthesis · Nucleotide synthesis: Purine + thymidylate synthesis
pathway: The MTHFR bypass — bioactive folate for methylation-dependent variants

name: Methylcobalamin (Active B12)
desc: Methylcobalamin is one of two active B12 forms (the other is adenosylcobalamin) used directly by cells without the reductase steps needed for cyanocobalamin conversion. Real evidence for correcting B12 deficiency and neurologic symptoms — a well-defined deficiency syndrome; supplementation-in-adequate-people evidence is thinner. Standard dose 500–1,000 mcg/day sublingual (bypasses intrinsic factor uptake issues that develop with age). Deficiency is common after 60 due to atrophic gastritis and PPI use.
mechanism: Methionine synthase: Methyl-B12 → Hcy remethylation to methionine → SAM · Myelin synthesis: Required for SAM-dependent myelin basic protein methylation · DNA methylation: SAM cycle input · Odd-chain FA oxidation: Adenosyl-B12 → methylmalonyl-CoA metabolism · Neurotransmitter methylation: Norepinephrine, serotonin, dopamine methylation
pathway: Direct-active B12 for age-related atrophic gastritis and methylation stacks

name: P5P (Pyridoxal-5-Phosphate, Active B6)
desc: P5P is the active coenzyme form of vitamin B6, cofactor for 150+ enzymes including homocysteine transsulfuration, neurotransmitter synthesis (GABA, serotonin, dopamine), and heme synthesis. Bypasses the hepatic conversion step needed for pyridoxine HCl (which is impaired in liver disease and by some medications). Standard dose 10–50 mg P5P/day. Chronic high-dose pyridoxine (>200 mg/day) can cause peripheral neuropathy; P5P appears less neurotoxic but keep intake below 100 mg/day.
mechanism: Homocysteine transsulfuration: P5P + CBS → cystathionine → cysteine → GSH · Neurotransmitter synthesis: P5P + AADC → dopamine, serotonin from L-DOPA / 5-HTP · GABA synthesis: P5P + GAD → GABA from glutamate · Heme synthesis: P5P + ALA synthase → aminolevulinic acid · Amino acid transamination: P5P + ALT/AST → glucogenic amino acid entry
pathway: The direct-active B6 coenzyme — bypass hepatic conversion, cofactor for 150+ enzymes

name: Benfotiamine (Fat-Soluble B1)
desc: Benfotiamine is a fat-soluble thiamine (B1) derivative with ~5× the bioavailability of thiamine HCl. Real RCT evidence for diabetic peripheral neuropathy symptom reduction (Stracke 2001 PMID 11289661; BENFO trial) and blocking three of the major AGE-formation pathways via transketolase activation. Standard dose 300–600 mg/day. Particularly valuable for chronic hyperglycemia states — target the mechanism that drives AGE-mediated aging.
mechanism: Transketolase activation: Shunts glucose from AGE-forming pathways into pentose phosphate · AGE prevention: Reduces methylglyoxal, CML, pentosidine formation · Polyol pathway ↓: Reduces sorbitol accumulation in nerves · Hexosamine pathway ↓: Reduces O-GlcNAc → improved insulin signaling · PKC ↓: Reduces vascular endothelial dysfunction
pathway: Transketolase activator that blocks all four AGE-formation pathways in hyperglycemia

name: Niacin (Nicotinic Acid, Vitamin B3)
desc: Niacin (nicotinic acid) is the flush-inducing B3 form with the strongest human lipid-modifying evidence of any OTC supplement — raises HDL 15–35%, lowers LDL 5–25%, lowers Lp(a) 20–30% (Coronary Drug Project 1975, PMID 1105674). BUT: the AIM-HIGH and HPS2-THRIVE trials showed niacin + statin did NOT reduce cardiovascular events despite improving lipid panel, and added serious adverse events. Also a NAD+ precursor. Standard OTC dose 500–2,000 mg/day; the flush and hepatotoxicity issues make this a pharmaceutical-grade decision, not a casual supplement.
mechanism: GPR109A → adipocyte: ↓ Lipolysis → ↓ FFA delivery → ↓ VLDL synthesis → ↓ LDL, ↓ TG · HDL raising: ↓ CETP; ↑ ApoA-I stability · Lp(a) lowering: Mechanism uncertain; niacin uniquely effective (~20–30% reduction) · NAD+ precursor: Preiss-Handler pathway → NAD+ · Flush: GPR109A on Langerhans → COX-1 → PGD2 → vasodilation
pathway: The lipid-modifying B3 form — dramatically raises HDL and lowers Lp(a), but AIM-HIGH/HPS2-THRIVE were negative

name: Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
desc: Vitamin C is essential (humans lack GULO gene → cannot synthesize it), cofactor for collagen hydroxylation, carnitine synthesis, and neurotransmitter synthesis. RDA (75–90 mg) prevents scurvy; longevity-optimizing intake sits at 200–500 mg/day (matches plasma saturation). High-dose IV (Rx, 10–100 g) is a different intervention (pharmacologic effect via H₂O₂ generation, oncology-adjunct research). Standard oral dose 500–1,000 mg/day divided; higher doses just get excreted.
mechanism: Collagen synthesis: Cofactor for prolyl/lysyl hydroxylases · Neurotransmitter synthesis: Dopamine β-hydroxylase → norepinephrine · Carnitine synthesis: Two of four enzymes require ascorbate · Vitamin E recycling: Reduces tocopheroxyl radical · Iron absorption: Reduces Fe³⁺ → Fe²⁺, enhances non-heme iron absorption · IV pharmacologic dose: Extracellular H₂O₂ generation (oncology research)
pathway: Essential cofactor for collagen and neurotransmitter synthesis; PHS-II negative for CV prevention

name: Mixed Tocopherols (Full-Spectrum Vitamin E)
desc: Vitamin E is a family of 8 compounds (α, β, γ, δ tocopherols + tocotrienols). Isolated high-dose α-tocopherol shows no benefit and possible harm in prevention trials (SELECT 2011 PMID 21990298 — increased prostate cancer risk at 400 IU/day). Mixed tocopherols with γ-tocopherol preserved (400 mg/day total, with ≥100 mg γ) is the better-evidenced form for lipid peroxidation control. Standard dose 200–400 mg mixed tocopherols/day with food.
mechanism: Membrane antioxidant: Chain-breaking radical trap in lipid bilayer · Vitamin E recycling: Vitamin C regenerates tocopherol from radical form · γ-tocopherol specific: Scavenges peroxynitrite (RNS), activates Nrf2 · Anti-atherogenic (weak): Reduces oxidized LDL in vitro; failed to translate to RCT outcomes · PKC modulation: α-tocopherol inhibits PKC in vascular smooth muscle
pathway: Preserve γ-tocopherol — SELECT and Miller meta made isolated α-tocopherol a bad bet

name: Iodine
desc: Iodine is essential — the substrate for thyroid hormones T3 and T4. Deficiency remains the world's leading preventable cause of intellectual disability; even mild deficiency in developed countries causes subclinical hypothyroidism, goiter, and cognitive underperformance. RDA 150 mcg/day (220 mcg pregnancy, 290 mcg lactation). Non-iodized-salt diet + low seafood/dairy = at-risk profile. Supplement 150–300 mcg/day (kelp or potassium iodide). Excess (>1,100 mcg/day) triggers Wolff-Chaikoff effect → thyroid dysfunction.
mechanism: Thyroid hormone synthesis: Iodide → iodinated tyrosine → T3, T4 · BMR regulation: T3 → nuclear TR → transcription of ~200 genes · Mitochondrial biogenesis: T3 → PGC-1α → mitochondrial genes · Brain development: Critical in first 1,000 days · Mammary function: Concentrated in ductal cells; fibrocystic disease link · Anti-microbial: Historical topical use (povidone-iodine) — different context
pathway: Essential thyroid substrate — deficiency is quietly returning as iodized salt use falls

name: HMB (β-Hydroxy β-Methylbutyrate)
desc: HMB is a leucine metabolite (~5% of dietary leucine is metabolized to HMB) with the strongest RCT evidence of any supplement for **preventing muscle loss during bed rest, hospitalization, and sarcopenia** — Deutz 2013 (PMID 23809521) 10-day bed rest in older adults showed HMB fully prevented lean mass loss vs 2.05 kg loss on placebo. Standard dose 3 g/day (as calcium-HMB or free-acid HMB). Not for young trained athletes seeking hypertrophy — the RCTs there are underwhelming. The signal is in preventing loss, not building excess.
mechanism: Ubiquitin-proteasome inhibition: ↓ MuRF-1, atrogin-1 → less muscle protein degradation · Sarcolemmal membrane stability: Precursor to cholesterol in muscle → membrane integrity · mTOR modulation: Weak agonist; less potent than leucine · Anti-inflammatory: ↓ TNF-α, IL-6 in muscle biopsy · Satellite cell function: Preclinical evidence of ↑ satellite cell activation
pathway: The strongest RCT evidence for preventing muscle loss during bed rest, hospitalization, and sarcopenia
timingRaw: Split with meals across the day

name: Trigonelline (Frontier NAD+ Precursor)
desc: Trigonelline is a natural pyridine alkaloid (found in coffee, fenugreek, and human plasma) that Nestlé Research identified in 2023–2024 as an under-appreciated **NAD+ precursor** that rises with age in centenarians. The landmark human proof-of-concept (Membrez / Auwerx, Nature Metabolism 2024, PMID 38286830) showed trigonelline restored NAD+ pools and improved muscle mitochondrial function in older adults. Standard emerging protocol 100–300 mg/day. Genuine new player in the NAD+ landscape — not just another repackaged NR.
mechanism: NAPRT → NaMN → NaAD → NAD+: Direct precursor via Preiss-Handler pathway · Bypasses NAMPT: Age-declining rate-limiting NMN synthesis step · Mitochondrial biogenesis: ↑ Muscle mitochondrial density in Membrez 2024 · SIRT1/3 substrate provision: Feeds sirtuin deacetylase activity · CD38 substrate competition: May reduce NAD+ consumption by inflammatory CD38
pathway: The 2024 NAD+ story — elevated in centenarians, restores muscle mitochondrial function in aged models

name: Krill Oil (Phospholipid Omega-3)
desc: Krill oil delivers omega-3 EPA/DHA bound to phospholipids (mostly phosphatidylcholine) plus astaxanthin. Per gram it contains less EPA+DHA than fish oil, but the phospholipid form has ~50% higher bioavailability per mg omega-3 (Ulven 2011 PMID 21688839). Small RCTs support lipid modification and mild joint benefit. Standard dose 1–3 g/day; more expensive than fish oil. Not a superior replacement, but a legitimate alternative for those who don't tolerate fish oil burps.
mechanism: Phospholipid form absorption: Direct membrane incorporation; higher bioavailability · Membrane omega-3 index: Raises RBC EPA+DHA% (goal >8%) · Anti-inflammatory eicosanoids: EPA → resolvins, protectins (SPMs) · Lipid modulation: ↓ TG, ↑ HDL via LXR / PPARα · Astaxanthin bonus: Lipophilic antioxidant
pathway: Phospholipid-bound EPA/DHA plus astaxanthin — higher bioavailability per mg than fish oil

name: PEA (Palmitoylethanolamide)
desc: Palmitoylethanolamide is an endogenous fatty acid amide, mechanistically an "endocannabinoid without the CB1 receptor" — a PPAR-α agonist and mast-cell-modulator with real RCT meta-analytic evidence for **chronic pain** (Paladini 2016 meta PMID 26890198 — pooled pain reduction ~2 points on 10-point scale) and preliminary neuroprotection data. Standard dose 300–1,200 mg/day of ultra-micronized PEA. Well tolerated, non-psychoactive, and one of the more legitimate pain-mechanism supplements.
mechanism: PPAR-α activation: Same nuclear receptor as fibrates → anti-inflammatory gene program · GPR55 modulation: Anti-inflammatory G-protein signaling · Mast cell stabilization: ↓ Degranulation → ↓ tissue histamine, tryptase, cytokines · FAAH inhibition: Prolongs endogenous anandamide → CB1/CB2 potentiation · Neuroprotection: Microglial modulation in preclinical AD/PD models
pathway: Endogenous PPAR-α agonist — "endocannabinoid without CB1" with real meta-analytic pain evidence

name: L-Arginine
desc: L-Arginine is the substrate for endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) — the enzyme that produces nitric oxide (NO) to relax blood vessels. Real RCT evidence for mild blood pressure reduction, endothelial dysfunction improvement, and erectile dysfunction. **Post-MI use is contraindicated** — the VINTAGE-MI trial (Schulman 2006 PMID 16391215) showed increased mortality in myocardial infarction survivors given arginine. Standard dose 3–6 g/day, but citrulline is often a better choice (higher plasma arginine per dose, better GI tolerance).
mechanism: eNOS substrate: L-Arginine → NO + L-citrulline (via eNOS) · Endothelium-dependent vasodilation: NO → cGMP → smooth muscle relaxation · Growth hormone (mild): Arginine acutely stimulates pituitary GH release · Urea cycle: Substrate for hepatic urea cycle · Arginase substrate: Competing pathway; consumes arginine, produces polyamines
pathway: eNOS substrate for endothelial NO — but VINTAGE-MI is a hard post-MI contraindication

name: Acetyl-L-Carnitine (ALCAR)
desc: Acetyl-L-carnitine is the acetylated form of carnitine that crosses the blood-brain barrier and delivers both a carnitine unit (fatty acid mitochondrial transport) and an acetyl group (acetylcholine synthesis substrate). RCT evidence for **diabetic peripheral neuropathy** (Sima 2005 PMID 15616239), **mild cognitive impairment / early Alzheimer's** (Montgomery 2003 meta PMID 12766374), and **depression augmentation** (Wang 2014 meta PMID 24451335). Standard dose 1,500–3,000 mg/day divided. Avoid PM dosing — can be alerting.
mechanism: Fatty acid oxidation: CPT1/2 shuttle — carnitine required for LCFA → mitochondrial matrix · Acetylcholine synthesis: Acetyl group + choline (via ChAT) → ACh · NGF signaling: ALCAR upregulates nerve growth factor receptor expression · Anti-neuroinflammatory: Reduces microglial activation in preclinical models · Mitochondrial biogenesis: Preclinical PGC-1α upregulation · Anti-apoptotic (neurons): Reduces caspase-3 activation
pathway: Brain-penetrant carnitine — Tier B for DPN, MCI, and depression with a large evidence base
